A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AMPD research. The text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–B support reliable comparison, including matching material across renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: Section 7 and Appendices A–B report original serving experiments, component ablations, parameter sensitivity, latency measurements, and deployment-planning evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical evaluations and adds scheduling-overhead measurements, further sensitivity results, and experiments under stricter SLO thresholds.

M1.justification: Adaptive routing, prefill reordering, KV-cache handling, and offline deployment planning remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 retain the same procedures. Chunked prefill and dynamic replanning are proposed as future work, not implemented additions.

E1.justification: Both versions use ToolBench, GAIA, HotpotQA, and DuReader traces for the same agentic and iterative-retrieval workloads. The added analyses reuse this coverage; stricter latency thresholds and another sensitivity configuration change evaluation settings rather than datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain Dynamo, vLLM, and vLLM-Continuum. The new stricter-SLO comparisons use the same set. Newly discussed related systems are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 retains the original protocols and adds Llama3.1-70B/DuReader evaluations at TTFT/ITL limits of 4000/45, 3000/45, and 3000/30 ms, alongside the retained 5000/50 ms setting. Figure 8 also adds a Qwen3-32B/HotpotQA sensitivity configuration at 1.2 requests/s.

E4.justification: v2 adds focused analyses of estimated KV-transfer cost relative to prefill computation (Figure 3), measured scheduling overhead (Section 7.2), sensitivity on a second model/workload combination (Figure 8), and robustness to stricter SLO thresholds (Figure 11). The existing component ablations and planner-validation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bars for these experiments. The new averages and workload proportions do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports average routing overhead of 0.39 ms, including 0.15 ms for metadata reading, and reordering overhead of 0.45 ms, plus KV-transfer ratios, additional sensitivity values, and stricter-SLO curves. The redrawn latency breakdown also slightly changes vLLM-Continuum TTFT bars (v1 Figure 4 versus v2 Figure 6). The main SLO comparisons, headline gains, planning results, and appendix end-to-end latency curves are retained.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(5), scheduling definitions, and the deployment-planning optimization remain unchanged. The added explanation of when P95 latency may poorly represent SLO attainment is qualitative; no new theorem, proof, or mathematical correction is provided.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and concluding research claims retain the same adaptive-scheduling and deployment-planning contributions. The claimed average SLO-attainment improvements of 67.29%–339.74% are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix A.3 expands the existing surrogate-objective caveat by explaining failure at extremely strict or loose SLO thresholds. Section 8 newly discusses deployment becoming suboptimal under workload or hardware changes, and proposes chunked prefill and background replanning with rolling migration as future remedies.

D1.justification: Section 7.2 newly states that adaptive routing and prefill reordering execute on CPU and overlap GPU computation, and provides component timing information. The implementation stack, hardware, default hyperparameters, simulator description, trace-generation instructions, and data-access links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion of joint aggregation/disaggregation approaches by Ruan et al. and Wang et al., explaining their claimed mismatch with heavier multi-round prefill workloads. Additional references cover chunked prefill and other serving and retrieval work, while the main research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Most prose and the section sequence are retained. v2 adds focused explanatory paragraphs, expands Section 8 into conclusions and future work, adds acknowledgments and an impact statement, and updates affiliations and the publication footer.

P2.justification: v1 Figure 4 is separated into the main comparison in v2 Figure 5 and a larger, reorganized latency breakdown in Figure 6. v2 adds Figures 3 and 11, expands the sensitivity figure with another row, and wraps text around the planning-time plot. Existing tables and most plots retain their structure.

improvement.justification: v2 supports previously qualitative scheduling-overhead assertions with measurements and adds targeted sensitivity and stricter-SLO checks. The expanded planner limitations and clearer latency breakdown improve transparency and readability. These gains strengthen the existing paper without substantially changing its central method or benchmark evidence.
